mainTopic: The ברייתא on ויקרא 4:20 (פר העלם דבר של ציבור): which offerings are done the same way, and which parts of the service are required for the offering to work.
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא that explains the words of ויקרא 4:20, about the bull brought when the community sins by mistake because of a wrong ruling. First the verse is used to include two other offerings done the same way: the פר כהן משיח and the שעירי עבודה זרה. Then the word 'לו' leaves out the שעירי הרגלים and the שעירי ראשי חדשים. The ברייתא asks why one group is included and the other left out. The answer is that we include offerings that atone for breaking a known מצוה, just like the community's bull. Next, the words 'וכפר' and 'ונסלח' teach that the atonement still works even without סמיכה or the שירים. Finally the ברייתא asks why the הזאות are required while סמיכה and שירים are not. The answer is that הזאות hold up the offering everywhere, while סמיכה and שירים never hold it up anywhere.

steps.title: Including the anointed priest's bull and the idol-worship goats
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads 'כאשר עשה לפר' as including the פר כהן משיח, and 'החטאת' as including the שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'As he did with the bull' means the bull of the anointed כהן גדול. 'The sin offering' means the goats brought for a communal mistake about idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps reading the verse word by word. Each phrase adds another offering that follows the same procedure as the community's bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כאשר עשה לפר' points back to a bull already described in the תורה, the פר כהן משיח. So that bull's sprinklings are also required. 'החטאת' adds the שעירי עבודה זרה, so they are offered the same inside way as the community's bull.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought by the anointed כהן גדול when he sins by mistake
The goats brought when the community worships idols by mistake
Sin offering

phrases.english: "As he did with the bull" —
this is the bull of the anointed priest.
"The sin offering" —
these are the goats for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה לְפַר זֶה פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's word-by-word reading of ויקרא 4:20 from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר כהן משיח and the שעירי עבודה זרה follow the same procedure as the פר העלם דבר של ציבור.

steps.title: Excluding the Festival and New Moon goats
steps.stepSummary: One might think the שעירי הרגלים and שעירי ראשי חדשים are included too, but the word 'לו' leaves them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should also include the goats of the Festivals and of ראש חודש. That is why the verse says 'to it,' meaning only this kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe other communal goats are included too. Then it blocks that idea from the word 'לו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Festival and ראש חודש goats are also communal sin offerings, so it is natural to think they belong in the group. The word 'לו' limits the procedure to 'it', so they are left out and are not done inside the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think', which introduces a wrong idea the ברייתא is about to reject
The goats offered on the Festivals
The goats offered on ראש חודש
'The verse teaches', which introduces the word that proves the point

phrases.english: One might think that I include
even the goats of the Festivals
and the goats of the New Moons?
The verse states: "to it."
phrases.notes: This is from 'כן יעשה לו', 'so shall he do to it', which limits the rule to this kind of offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף שְׂעִירֵי הָרְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on the inclusion from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שעירי הרגלים and שעירי ראשי חדשים are left out by the word 'לו'.

steps.title: Why include one group and exclude the other?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason we have to include the idol-worship goats and leave out the Festival and New Moon goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: What made you decide to include these and leave out those?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how we know which goats go in which group. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse has a word that includes ('החטאת') and a word that leaves out ('לו'). But it never says which goats go with which word. We need a reason so the choice is not random.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What did you see', meaning what is your reason for this choice
To include
To exclude, to leave out

phrases.english: And what did you see
to include these
and to exclude those?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת אֵלּוּ וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how steps 1 and 2 sorted the goats into two groups.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reason there is for putting the עבודה זרה goats in the included group and the Festival and New Moon goats in the excluded group.

steps.title: We include offerings that atone for a known sin
steps.stepSummary: The idol-worship goats are included because they atone for breaking a known מצוה, just like the community's bull. The Festival and New Moon goats do not, so they are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the verse both included and excluded, I include the ones that atone for breaking a known מצוה, and I leave out the ones that do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. It sorts the goats by whether they atone for a specific, known sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The community's bull atones for a known mistake about a specific מצוה. The עבודה זרה goats also atone for a known sin, idol worship, so they are similar to it. The Festival and ראש חודש goats atone for something that was never known, so they are not similar and are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse included and excluded
They atone
Breaking a known, specific מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: The test for joining the group is likeness to the community's bull: the offering must atone for a known sin about a specific מצוה.

phrases.english: Since the verse included and excluded,
I include these
which atone for the transgression of a known מצוה,
and I exclude those

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מְכַפְּרִין עַל עֲבֵירַת מִצְוָה יְדוּעָה.
phrases.english: which do not atone for the transgression of a known מצוה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Offerings that atone for a known sin are like the community's bull and are included. The others are left out.

steps.title: Atonement works even without סמיכה or שירים
steps.stepSummary: 'וכפר' teaches that atonement works even without סמיכה. 'ונסלח' teaches it works even if the שירים were not put on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall atone' means even if there was no leaning of hands. 'And it shall be forgiven' means even if the leftover blood was not put on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to reading the verse. It shows that two parts of the service are not required for the offering to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the ברייתא has taught which steps are required. Now 'וכפר' and 'ונסלח' teach the opposite: the atonement still happens without סמיכה and without the שירים. These are still מצוות to do, but missing them does not ruin the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall atone'
Leaning hands on the animal's head
'And it shall be forgiven'
The leftover blood, poured on the base of the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean סמיכה and שירים are optional to begin with. They are still required as מצוות. They just do not stop the atonement if they were left out.

phrases.english: "And he shall atone" —
even if he did not lean his hands.
"And it shall be forgiven" —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן שִׁירַיִם.
phrases.english: even if he did not put the remainder of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִפֶּר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא סָמַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's reading of the verse after the side question of steps 3 and 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving out סמיכה or the שירים does not stop the atonement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contrast in the next step: some parts of the service are required for the offering to work, and some are not.

steps.title: Why are the sprinklings required but not סמיכה and שירים?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason we have to say the הזאות are required, while missing סמיכה or שירים still leaves the offering valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What made you decide that the offering is invalid without the sprinklings, but valid without leaning and leftover blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a new question about how it sorted the parts of the service. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse has words that make things required ('ועשה... כאשר עשה') and words that do not ('וכפר', 'ונסלח'). But it never names which parts of the service go with which words. The question asks why the הזאות go in the required group, and סמיכה and שירים in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: To disqualify, to make the offering invalid
The sprinklings of blood
To make valid

phrases.english: And what did you see to disqualify regarding the sprinklings,
and to render it valid regarding leaning and the remainder of the blood?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לִפְסוֹל בְּהַזָּאוֹת וּלְהַכְשִׁיר בִּסְמִיכָה וְשִׁירַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how step 5 split the parts of the service between required and not required.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the הזאות are required for the offering to work, while סמיכה and שירים are not.

steps.title: Sprinklings are always required, hand-placing and leftover blood are not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the הזאות hold up the offering here because they hold up the offering everywhere. סמיכה and שירים do not generally hold up an offering, so they do not hold it up here either.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say: I disqualify the offering if the sprinklings are missing, because sprinklings hold up the offering everywhere. I let the offering stay valid if the hand-placing or the leftover blood is missing, because those do not hold up the offering in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question from step 6. It explains why the הזאות must be done, while missing סמיכה or שירים still leaves the offering valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed from the פסוק that the offering works even without סמיכה or the שירים. The question was why the הזאות should be any different. The answer is that we follow the general rule found in all other offerings: הזאות always hold up the offering, and סמיכה and שירים generally don't. Rashi spells it out: סמיכה doesn't hold up an offering anywhere, and pouring out the leftover blood doesn't hold up an outer חטאת, according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold back or prevent. If a step is מעכב, the offering does not work without it.
Disqualify, make the offering invalid
Declare fit, keep the offering valid
Everywhere, in all cases

steps.whatToRemember: The rule follows the general pattern found everywhere: הזאות always hold up the offering, so they are required here too. סמיכה and שירים generally don't hold it up, so the offering is valid without them.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that סמיכה and שירים should not be done. They are still a מצוה. The point is only that, after the fact, the offering still works if they were left out.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a simple method the ברייתא uses: when it is unclear whether a step is required, look at how that same step is treated in all other cases.

phrases.english: You can say: I disqualify the offering if the sprinklings are missing
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; the corrected wording adds it.

phrases.english: because they hold up the offering everywhere,
phrases.notes: "Everywhere" means in every offering that has these sprinklings. Without them, the offering does not work.

phrases.english: and I declare the offering fit if the hand-placing or the leftover blood is missing
because they do not hold up the offering in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הזאות are required because they are required in all cases. סמיכה and שירים are not generally required, so the offering stays valid without them.
